quotes.text: The Family Card is a database-driven digital identification and social protection instrument designed to deliver regular financial assistance directly to vulnerable households.
Proxy Means Test (PMT) scoring + door-to-door data collection

The government has set a target to collect data from an estimated 4.45 crore families and add them to a database by December, as nationwide data collection under the Family Card programme began today.

During the pilot phase, which ran through June 2026, data was collected from 112,094 families in 57 units across 55 upazilas and city corporation areas in 44 districts under all eight divisions, he said.
Based on Proxy Means Test scores, 71,831 eligible beneficiaries were selected and provided with family cards and allowances.

The government aims to bring 1.61 crore families under the Family Card scheme by 2030 and will distribute 41 lakh new cards nationwide in the current 2026-27 fiscal year, said State Minister for Social Welfare Farzana Sharmin Putul today (14 July).
A total of 66,815 trained data collectors and 6,681 supervisors have been deployed for this task. The data collection process is scheduled to conclude by November 30 and it will be ready by December.

He said, initially out of 45 million households between 16 million and 21 million families categorized as ultra-poor, poor or low-income will be identified as eligible for the allowance based on their PMT scores.
